"Raymond III Count of Tripoli was a notable noble of the Crusader states in the twelfth century. He was born around 1140 to Raymond II Count of Tripoli and Hodierna daughter of King Baldwin II of Jerusalem. His early years were marked by the loss of his father who was assassinated in 1152. After his father's death Raymond III inherited the county while still a minor. He was placed under the regency of his mother and later under the guardianship of the King of Jerusalem. *Early Life and Ascension* highlights how he grew up in the turbulent court of Tripoli and learned the arts of war and diplomacy. Upon reaching adulthood he began to assert his authority over the county and sought to expand his influence in the northern Levant. He forged alliances with neighboring powers such as the Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia and the County of Edessa. He also faced pressure from the growing strength of the Muslim forces under Nur ad Din and later Saladin. *Political Role and Conflicts* describes his frequent clashes with the King of Jerusalem especially with Guy of Lusignan whom he viewed as a threat to the independence of Tripoli. Raymond III opposed the Lusignan succession and supported the claim of Isabella and her husband Conrad of Montferrat. His opposition led to a tense standoff that culminated in the Battle of Hattin in 1187 where the Crusader army suffered a devastating defeat. Although Raymond III escaped the battlefield he retreated to Tripoli and worked to organize the defense of his city. *Later Years and Death* covers his efforts to strengthen the fortifications of Tripoli and to negotiate with Saladin for a possible truce. Despite his attempts the fall of Jerusalem and the loss of other Crusader strongholds weakened his position. Raymond III died in 1187 shortly after the Battle of Hattin leaving his young son Raymond IV as heir. The county of Tripoli continued to exist for several more decades under the rule of his descendants before eventually falling to the Mamluks. His legacy is remembered as that of a prudent lord who tried to balance Crusader ideals with the harsh realities of frontier warfare."
